GRANULARITY JUSTIFICATION (operator-delegated survey call, WAL 1201; the schema-conformant evidence.granularity_check object carries only its three required fields, so the reasoning lives here exactly as in the phase_14 precedent): OPERATOR-DELEGATED CALL (WAL 1201: 'EVALUATE whether to split issues finer/more to ensure rigorous completion'). N=4, split by DELIVERABLE AND FILE OWNERSHIP, not by defect label. batch_size = min(5, max(1, ceil(4/3))) = 2, so the cards were generated in 2 batches of 2 ([t99,t100] then [t101,t102]), each card written in its own write call, all writes of a batch completed before the next started. WHY THE ANCHOR DEBT IS TWO CARDS AND NOT ONE: it is measurably two premise families - the index-side stale byte-pin literal inside stored legs 190/191 (an orchestrator-applied amendment RECORD on the t96 coordinated-set precedent, predicted baseline effect ZERO) versus the generator-side stale constant at docs_verification.py:46 (a product-code edit with a committed-report regeneration and the milestone's only predicted baseline change 33 to 32). Different files, different delivery mechanisms, different verification surfaces, different baseline arithmetic; merging them would put an orchestrator-owned delivery and a product edit inside one merge-window verdict. WHY IT IS NOT FINER THAN TWO: each half is a single-literal substitution with exactly one measurable each; splitting the index side per leg (190, 191) would produce two cards whose entire content is one line of the same coordinated record, which the t96 {232,250} precedent explicitly handles as ONE coordinated set. WHY B1 PLUS B3 ARE ONE CARD (t101): they are two wrong expectations inside ONE closed artifact - t95's ac5 expectation list and ac6's as-stored pin table - i.e. one fence family; splitting them would force two re-groom/ac_hash passes over the same one closed t95 fence for zero added observability, and the t96 lesson is that entangled premises travel together. Per-defect rigor is preserved by separate ACs and a per-defect record entry, which is where observability actually lives. WHY B2 IS ITS OWN CARD (t102): a different deliverable CLASS - a pollution-boundary change to the in-repo verifier (SKIP_DIRS += build, scratch, plus report regeneration) and a recorded discipline for orchestrator-side sweep tooling that no card in this repo can patch - not a t95 fence premise. WHY t102 IS NOT MERGED INTO t100 despite the shared file: the single-writer rule forces them SEQUENTIAL (t102 depends t100) rather than merged, because they change different concerns of docs_verification.py (anchor constant versus walk boundary) and each needs its own regeneration/invariance measurement; merging would double one card's diff and blur which measurement belongs to which premise. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: N=2 (one anchor card plus one t95 card) would mix an orchestrator-owned amendment record with a product-code edit and hide the 33-to-32 baseline change inside a mixed verdict; N=6 (per-leg and per-defect cards) would create two cards whose entire content is one line of one coordinated record and force redundant ac_hash churn on a closed artifact. FILE COUNTS PER CARD: t99 = 1 (the amendment record), t100 = 2 (generator plus regenerated report), t101 = 1 (the premise-correction record), t102 = 3 (generator line, regenerated report, policy record) so max_files_per_issue = 3, under the configured max_files 4. AC DRAFTS ARE CAPPED AT 6 PER CARD (the configured max_acs 6): t101 and t102 were drafted at 7 and their redundant purity/baseline legs merged, so no card exceeds the limit. Card PROSE bodies are long by design (measured base state plus constraints), but the PRODUCT diffs are small and bounded: t99 about 40 JSON lines, t100 a 1-line constant plus a regenerated report, t101 about 60 JSON lines, t102 a 1-line constant plus report plus about 80 lines of record - all under the 300-diff-line limit, so within_limits is TRUE (warn_only:true regardless; unlike phase_13/phase_14 no card here is an evidence-capture body).
